editorial:
Imagine waking up in a world that feels a bit off, where the silence says more than the dialogue. You are dropped into the life of a character who feels trapped by their own reality and just wants to escape into something lighter and more free. The vibe is very quiet and moody, focusing on the small, strange moments that make up a person's day. It feels like a dream you can't quite remember, making you feel the same confusion and longing that the main character is going through as they navigate their surroundings.

What really works here is how the director uses simple shots to show big emotions. The acting is understated, which keeps things feeling real and grounded. While it moves slowly and might feel too quiet for some, it is perfect if you want something that makes you think. It is a great pick for people who enjoy artistic shorts that leave you feeling a bit thoughtful after the credits roll.
endingExplained: The story wraps up by showing that the desire to be something else is more of a feeling than a real possibility. You see the character realize that they cannot actually change their nature or fly away from their problems. The final scenes show them returning to their normal, dull life, but with a new sense of sadness. It ends on a quiet note, leaving you to wonder if they will ever find true peace.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quiet stories and artistic short films.
